values.goal: Call actual Wasm modules and distinguish linear memory·copying·numeric representation·initialization costs.
values.capstone: Validate array transformations in JS and actual Wasm, then decide whether to adopt Wasm using cold·warm·copy-inclusive end-to-end latency.

values.title: Modules and Linear Memory
values.prerequisites: Understand JavaScript·TypedArray and the basics of the chosen compiled language, and be able to read the inputs and outputs of the existing starting examples.
values.environment: The iframe preview is an experiment with WebAssembly.Memory and JS reference computations; do not present it as execution of an actual Wasm module. Practice with actual modules in a separate Node 22+ environment or a controlled local web project. Use kernel.wat·kernel.wasm·benchmark.mjs in the existing src/labs/webassembly-02·03 folders, and rebuild with the official wat2wasm tool when modifying WAT. Preserve CSP·isolation, and record measurements yourself.
values.concepts.0.title: Module boundary
values.concepts.0.explanation: Wasm calls exports of a compiled module. JS generally handles DOM manipulation.
values.concepts.1.title: Preview scope
values.concepts.1.explanation: The existing first example observes WebAssembly.Memory. It does not compile a module or accelerate computation.
values.outcomes.0: Learning outcome: explain the role of Module boundary. Input cases: [1,2,3] and an invalid file path.
values.outcomes.1: Deliverable: JS·Wasm sum 6 and a record of loading errors. Explain the rationale for handling Preview scope, linking it to the code.
values.steps.0: In day-1.mjs in a separate practice project, read the existing Memory example, then instantiate webassembly-02's kernel.wasm in a separate Node environment and call sum. Refer to the existing Unit 1·14·28 examples only as starting points.
values.steps.1: Input conditions: [1,2,3] and an invalid file path. Baseline: valid wasm. Run under the baseline conditions, then record observations and errors in notes/day-1.md.
values.steps.2: Variable: file path; changed value: missing file. Run again through the same input path. Deliverable to save: JS·Wasm sum 6 and a record of loading errors. Hypothesis to check: Normal results and loading failures are distinguished. Compare it with the actual results, and record whether they agree and why they differ.
values.variables.0.name: file path
values.variables.0.expected: Normal results and loading failures are distinguished.
values.criteria.0: Required deliverable: JS·Wasm sum 6 and a record of loading errors. Results are available for both the baseline and changed conditions, allowing comparison of 2 conditions; input values and the execution environment are recorded together.
values.criteria.1: The explanation of differences between the two conditions connects both concepts: Module boundary and Preview scope. For unexpected items, at least 1 cause or reason they remain unresolved is recorded.
values.questions.0: Which processing stage does Module boundary affect in this exercise? Input cases: [1,2,3] and an invalid file path.
values.questions.1: Variable: file path. Hypothesis to check: Normal results and loading failures are distinguished. Did the actual results agree with the hypothesis? Explain the evidence in terms of Preview scope.
values.references.0.title: WebAssembly Developer’s Guide
values.references.1.title: MDN WebAssembly JavaScript API
values.references.2.title: MDN WebAssembly.Memory

values.title: WAT and Binary

values.environment: First check the execution scope guidance on the example screen. The following describes the environment needed to extend the assignment in a separate project. The iframe preview is an experiment with WebAssembly.Memory and JS reference computations; do not present it as execution of an actual Wasm module. Practice with actual modules in a separate Node 22+ environment or a controlled local web project. Use kernel.wat·kernel.wasm·benchmark.mjs in the existing src/labs/webassembly-02·03 folders, and rebuild with the official wat2wasm tool when modifying WAT. Preserve CSP·isolation, and record measurements yourself.
values.concepts.0.title: Text format
values.concepts.0.explanation: WAT is a readable representation of module structure. Browsers do not directly execute a WAT string as a Wasm binary.
values.concepts.1.title: Build
values.concepts.1.explanation: wat2wasm converts text into binary. Check build results separately from execution results.
values.outcomes.0: Learning outcome: explain the role of Text format. Input cases: the existing sum function and a modified constant.
values.outcomes.1: Deliverable: build logs and export call results. Explain the rationale for handling Build, linking it to the code.
values.steps.0: In day-2.mjs in a separate practice project, copy kernel.wat into a separate folder and run the official tool: wat2wasm kernel.wat -o kernel.wasm. Refer to the existing Unit 1·14·28 examples only as starting points.
values.steps.1: Input conditions: the existing sum function and a modified constant. Baseline: valid WAT. Run under the baseline conditions, then record observations and errors in notes/day-2.md.
values.steps.2: Variable: source; changed value: WAT with a syntax error. Run again through the same input path. Deliverable to save: build logs and export call results. values.questions.0: Which processing stage does Text format affect in this exercise? Input cases: the existing sum function and a modified constant.
values.questions.1: Variable: source. Hypothesis to check: Syntax errors are exposed during the build. Did the actual results agree with the hypothesis? Explain the evidence in terms of Build.

values.concepts.0.title: Module
values.concepts.0.explanation: The result of compile is compiled code. Distinguish it from an instance with execution state.
values.concepts.1.title: Instance
values.concepts.1.explanation: Multiple instances can be created from the same module. Whether their memories are shared depends on the definitions.
values.outcomes.0: Learning outcome: explain the role of Module. Input cases: the same module and different first elements.
values.outcomes.1: Deliverable: the first element value for each instance. Explain the rationale for handling Instance, linking it to the code.
values.steps.0: In day-3.mjs in a separate practice project, create two instances after WebAssembly.compile and modify each memory. Refer to the existing Unit 1·14·28 examples only as starting points.
values.steps.1: Input conditions: the same module and different first elements. Baseline: one. Run under the baseline conditions, then record observations and errors in notes/day-3.md.
values.steps.2: Variable: instances; changed value: two. Run again through the same input path. Deliverable to save: the first element value for each instance. Hypothesis to check: Internally defined memory remains independent in each instance. Compare it with the actual results, and record whether they agree and why they differ.
